insights.insight: Ad tech sells inferred purchase intent at $5–$150 CPA; this protocol settles verified purchase confirmation at ~$0.10 per receipt — a 50–200x cost delta that isn't a marginal improvement, it eliminates the attribution problem entirely.

Etsy entering the top brand list on 2026-03-30 marks the first digital-native brand in the dataset, indicating the receipt corpus has expanded beyond physical retail into purchase confirmation emails — the natural expansion surface for any cookieless commerce signal strategy.

6,792 cryptographically verified receipts across 14 CBSAs with measurable brand and category entropy cannot be replicated by copying the pipeline — the competitive asset is the accumulated signal corpus, not the verification method.

A single cycle on 2026-03-29 added 19 new CBSAs (86.4% diffusion rate) after a complete quiet cycle, then contracted to 1 new CBSA — marketers should read burst-quiet cycles as network expansion behavior, not inconsistent data quality.

Week-over-week throughput has stayed below 1.0x for 11+ consecutive cycles while the growth rate compounds above 1.0x — the 7-day GMV window rose from $32,361 to $36,436 in one cycle, confirming momentum is building beneath suppressed surface activity.

insights.topic: Brand category drift as leading indicator
insights.insight: The top brand list has shifted from big-box anchors (Walmart, Home Depot) into specialty retail (Whole Foods, Total Wine) and now online marketplaces (Etsy), signaling that verified commerce coverage is tracking where consumer spending is actually diversifying.
